summary.result: The findings indicate that South Korea’s current timber supply structure reproduces asymmetrical relationships that undermine climate justice at the global level.
summary.background: South Korea relies on imported timber for more than 80 percent of its timber needs, raising ethical concerns about whether it is appropriate to conserve domestic forests while meeting national demand through the exploitation of forests in other countries, particularly in developing regions.
summary.method: Drawing on a qualitative review of policy documents and comparative international cases, the analysis illustrates how environmental burdens and carbon storage losses are externalized to developing countries under the prevailing discourse of domestic forest conservation.
